about.title: Gonzales Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Gonzales is a small town of about 8,473 people, and a sudden loss here is felt on every block. In 2025, Monterey County records show 8 injury collisions in the city and no traffic deaths, a count worth holding onto. Still, families in Gonzales do lose people, whether on US-101, along Alta Street, 5th Street or Fanoe Road, in the fields and packing operations that surround town, or under someone else's care. Public records note that local crashes cluster on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, and in some situations by other dependents or heirs. It runs separately from any criminal case, and it can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. California allows two years from the date of death to file, with a much shorter window if a public agency is involved. LawProactive simply introduces you to an attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Gonzales Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death, but claims against a city, county or state agency must be started much sooner. Connecting early protects that window.

items.title: Full accounting of what was lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash that killed my family member happened on US-101 near Gonzales. Does a criminal case stop us from filing a civil claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it can proceed whether or not the Monterey County District Attorney files charges. The civil case focuses on your family's losses rather than punishment. An attorney can explain how the two tracks may affect timing and evidence.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there are none, certain dependents or heirs may qualify. Because several relatives are often involved, families usually bring one combined action, and an attorney can help coordinate that.

items.question: How long do we have, and does it change if a government vehicle or road was involved?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a public entity such as the city, county, Caltrans or a school district may be responsible, a written claim must typically be presented within six months first. Missing that shorter step can end the case, so it is wise to speak with someone soon.
